explanation: In indirect speech, 'I' changes to 'he' and 'am going' changes to 'was going'. Present continuous changes to past continuous.
Present perfect 'have completed' changes to past perfect 'had completed' in indirect speech.
Universal truths don't change tense in indirect speech - 'revolves' remains 'revolves'.
In direct speech, 'told me' becomes 'said to me' and 'was feeling' becomes 'am feeling'.
Question word 'where' remains, but 'do you live' changes to 'I lived' (simple past).
'Will' changes to 'would' and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day' in indirect speech.
Negative imperative 'Don't' changes to 'forbade' in indirect speech.
Exclamatory sentences use 'exclaimed that' and 'what a' becomes 'very'.
Present perfect continuous changes to past perfect continuous, 'here' changes to 'there'.
Imperative sentences use 'ordered' + 'to + verb' in indirect speech.
Yes/No questions use 'if' or 'whether', 'can' changes to 'could'.
'Bought' (simple past) changes to 'had bought' (past perfect), 'this' changes to 'that', 'yesterday' changes to 'the previous day'.
Imperative sentences often use 'advised', 'told', or 'instructed' + 'to + verb'.
'May' changes to 'might' in indirect speech.
Requests use 'requested + object + to + verb' in indirect speech.
